problemStatement.formal: R(4,k) = Ω(k^{5/2}/polylog) and R(4,k) = O(k³/(log k)²)
problemStatement.plain: Formalize structural results about Ramsey numbers R(4,k), including the Paley graph construction for R(4,4) ≥ 18, the Wagner graph construction for R(3,4) ≥ 9, probabilistic lower bounds, and binomial coefficient upper bounds.
whyMatters: The R(4,k) gap between k^{5/2} and k^3 is a major open problem in Ramsey theory
The Paley graph construction connects algebraic number theory to combinatorics
Spencer's LLL improvement demonstrates power of the probabilistic method

proven: R(3,3) = 6 exactly (upper + lower bound fully proved)
R(3,4) ≥ 9 via Wagner graph W₈ (6 new theorems, all native_decide)
Paley graph on F_17: symmetry, no red K_4, no blue K_4 (all proved by native_decide)
R(4,4) > 16 via Paley graph (fully proved, no axioms)
Concrete upper bounds: R(3,3)=6, R(4,4)=20, R(5,5)=70, etc.
Structural: symmetry, monotonicity, Pascal's rule, positivity
R(r,s) ≥ s and R(r,s) ≥ r for appropriate bounds
open: Exact order of R(4,k): between k^{5/2} and k^3 (up to log factors)
knownResults.goal: All tractable results proved. 7 axioms remain (deep probabilistic/asymptotic).
